slides.title: Spot the difference.
slides.body: Two Land Rover Series IIA Station Wagons, a few years apart. Here's how to tell them apart in five seconds.

slides.title: Lamps in the grille panel.
slides.body: On early IIAs the headlamps sit inboard, either side of the grille. This one is a short-wheelbase 88.

slides.title: Lamps moved to the wings.
slides.body: From 1969 the headlamps moved out into the wings. The grille is still metal: the Series III got a plastic one.

slides.title: Count the windows.
slides.body: The long-wheelbase 109 Station Wagon adds a row of side windows behind the doors. The 88 is the short one.

end.title: Shopping for a Series?
end.body: Chassis rot, gearbox wear, swivels and every check worth doing, in our free Series buying guide.
